result.topic_en: Latin text from Riemann's Paris prize essay on heat conduction: invariance of the curvature expression, its geometric interpretation as curvature of a surface formed by shortest lines in an n-dimensional space, the case n=3 giving six conditions, and a closing remark that lack of time prevented carrying out the calculations.
result.transcription:
Pariser Aufgabe. 13

manere si in locos variationum $ds_\iota$, $\delta s_\iota$ expressiones ipsarum quaelibet
lineares independentes $a\,ds_\iota + b\,\delta s_\iota$, $c\,ds_\iota + d\,\delta s_\iota$ substituantur. Valores autem
maximi et minimi hujus functionis (III) ipsarum $ds_\iota$, $\delta s_\iota$ neque a forma
expressionis $\sum b_{\iota,\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$, neque a valoribus variationum $ds_\iota$, $\delta s_\iota$ pendebunt,
unde ex his valoribus dignosci poterit, an duae hujusmodi expressiones
in se transformari possint.

Disquisitiones hasce interpretatione quadam geometrica illustrare possumus,
quae quamquam conceptibus inusitatis nitatur, tamen obiter eam addigitavisse juvabit.

Expressio $\sqrt{\sum b_{\iota,\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}}$ spectari potest tanquam elementum lineare in
spatio generaliore $n$ dimensionum nostrum intuitum transcendente.
Quodsi in hoc spatio a puncto $(s_1, s_2 \dots s_n)$ ducantur omnes lineae brevissimae, in quarum elementis initialibus variationes ipsarum $s$ sunt ut
$\alpha ds_1 + \beta \delta s_1 : \alpha ds_2 + \beta \delta s_2 : \dots : \alpha ds_n + \beta \delta s_n$ denotantibus $\alpha$ et $\beta$ quantitates
quaslibet, hae lineae superficiem constituent, quam in spatium vulgare
nostro intuitui subjectum evolvere licet. Quo pacto expressio III erit mensura curvaturae hujus superficiei in puncto $(s_1, s_2 \dots s_n)$.

Si jam ad casum $n=3$ redimus, expressio II est forma secundi gradus ipsarum

$ds_2\delta s_3 - ds_3\delta s_2$, $ds_3\delta s_1 - ds_1\delta s_3$, $ds_1\delta s_2 - ds_2\delta s_1$

unde in hoc casu sex obtinemus aequationes, quibus functiones $b$ satisfacere debent, ut $\sum b_{\iota,\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$ in formam constantibus coefficientibus gaudentem transformari possit. Ope notionum modo expositarum, est demonstratu, has sex conditiones, ut hoc fieri possit, sufficere. Observandum
tamen est, tres tantum esse prorsus independentes.

Jam ut quaestionem ab Ill$^{ma}$ Academia propositam persolvamus,
in his sex aequationibus formae functionum $b$, methodo supra exposita
inventae, sunt substituendae, quo pacto omnes casus invenientur, in
quibus temperatura $u$ in corporibus homogeneis functio temporis et
duarum tantum variabilium fieri possit.

Sed angustia temporis non permisit, hos calculos perscribere.
Contenti igitur esse debemus, postquam methodos, quibus usi sumus,

methods.what: Invariance of the extremal values of curvature expression III under change of coordinates and choice of variations, giving a criterion for equivalence of quadratic forms
methods.quote:
Valores autem
maximi et minimi hujus functionis (III) ipsarum $ds_\iota$, $\delta s_\iota$ neque a forma
expressionis $\sum b_{\iota,\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$, neque a valoribus variationum $ds_\iota$, $\delta s_\iota$ pendebunt

methods.what: Interpretation of the quadratic form as line element of an n-dimensional space
methods.quote:
Expressio $\sqrt{\sum b_{\iota,\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}}$ spectari potest tanquam elementum lineare in
spatio generaliore $n$ dimensionum nostrum intuitum transcendente.

methods.what: Sectional curvature: expression III as Gaussian curvature of the surface formed by geodesics through a point in the plane spanned by two directions
methods.quote: Quo pacto expressio III erit mensura curvaturae hujus superficiei in puncto $(s_1, s_2 \dots s_n)$.

methods.what: For n=3 the curvature form II is quadratic in the bivector components, yielding six conditions for flatness (constant coefficients), of which three are independent
methods.quote: $ds_2\delta s_3 - ds_3\delta s_2$, $ds_3\delta s_1 - ds_1\delta s_3$, $ds_1\delta s_2 - ds_2\delta s_1$

methods.what: Method for solving the prize problem: substitute the forms of b into the six equations
methods.quote:
in his sex aequationibus formae functionum $b$, methodo supra exposita
inventae, sunt substituendae

items.quote: Ope notionum modo expositarum, est demonstratu, has sex conditiones, ut hoc fieri possit, sufficere.
items.english: By means of the notions just set out, it can be demonstrated that these six conditions suffice for this to be possible.

items.quote:
Observandum
tamen est, tres tantum esse prorsus independentes.
items.english: It should be observed, however, that only three are entirely independent.

items.quote:
Jam ut quaestionem ab Ill$^{ma}$ Academia propositam persolvamus,
in his sex aequationibus formae functionum $b$, methodo supra exposita
inventae, sunt substituendae, quo pacto omnes casus invenientur, in
quibus temperatura $u$ in corporibus homogeneis functio temporis et
duarum tantum variabilium fieri possit.
items.english: Now, to solve the question proposed by the most illustrious Academy, the forms of the functions b, found by the method set out above, must be substituted into these six equations; in this way all cases will be found in which the temperature u in homogeneous bodies can become a function of time and of only two variables.

items.quote: Sed angustia temporis non permisit, hos calculos perscribere.
items.english: But lack of time did not permit writing out these calculations.
